issue.title: Document Windows launcher's native symlink test prerequisite
issue.body:
Priority: P3. The permanent native launcher acceptance suite now verifies genuine junctions and directory symbolic links, but docs/10-testing-and-quality.md does not describe those cases or their host requirement. On Windows without directory-symlink creation capability, the suite fails at create-alias (EPERM on this host); it deliberately does not skip the required case. Hosted Windows passed both link types.

Acceptance:
- Update the native suite description in docs/10 with alias helper, cold/warm, refusal and cleanup coverage.
- Explain the required symlink-creation capability and that its absence is a failing prerequisite, not passing or skipped product evidence.
- Keep setup guidance consistent with actual supported Windows behavior, without requiring developers to weaken host security settings.

Deferred because this is developer test setup documentation, while behavior is documented in docs/09 and #435's full native acceptance has passed. Review finding R1.

Origin: Claude Opus 5.5 xhigh formal scan 1 of PR #492 at `6f383da798872aa0e6bd1e0de1fdcd4e702de9ae` (full report in the PR conversation). Open and closed issue searches for symlink, entry, inert and artifact found no matching root cause.

Disposition: DEFER-ISSUE; parked under `backlog`, with no pickup gate. This follow-up does not expand the authorized four-intent batch or block #435. Preserve docs/15 delivery and independent opposite-family review when separately dispatched.

issue.title: Strengthen the built launcher identity helper's inert-import control
issue.body:
Priority: P3. In the current built regression, the helper is imported under `node -e` with no script argv[1]. The native suite imports with a file-URL string in argv[1], which cannot resolve as a filesystem entry. Both correctly observe inert import, but neither built control exercises the comparison against a different existing entry file. The unit test covers that branch and every real gateway startup imports this helper from a different main file; no product defect is established.

Acceptance:
- Run a real wrapper entry file which imports the built helper through an alias, with invalid configuration to make accidental execution observable.
- Assert no helper stdout, no configuration evaluation and no store mutation; retain direct-execution positive/negative controls.
- Demonstrate the wrapper's actual argv[1] is a different existing file and test the intended regression without duplicating broad native runs.

Deferred because current correctness is established and this is a stronger focused regression control. Review finding R2.

issue.title: Diagnose repository check entry guards through aliased checkout paths
issue.body:
Priority: P2/P3 pending reproduction. `tooling/scripts/gen-docs.mjs`, `tooling/scripts/check-migrations.mjs` and `tooling/perf/summary.mjs` compare a resolved argv entry spelling with a loader-realpathed module URL. A self-contained Node 22.23.4 junction probe confirms these spellings can differ, making this lexical guard false. Actual pnpm invocation and repository gate bypass have NOT been reproduced. CI used real directories; no current CI result is invalidated by this observation.

Potential impact: invoking the scripts through an alias may exit zero before doing their work, including docs or migration checks.

Acceptance:
- Reproduce actual supported pnpm commands from a disposable aliased checkout, with deliberate invalid generated docs/migration inputs as discriminating negative controls.
- Record direct versus alias argv/cwd behavior and exit/output; distinguish a direct Node invocation from an actual pnpm gate path.
- If the defect is reachable, fix entry dispatch and add bounded regressions for each affected command; otherwise record why the actual invocation is safe and close with evidence.
- Preserve inert import and normal direct invocation; do not change gate thresholds or owner files.

Deferred because these are pre-existing tooling entry points outside #435's launcher helper contract. Review observation O1.

issue.title: Restore downloadable Windows launcher acceptance artifacts in CI
issue.body:
Priority: P3. The Windows launcher CI job's upload-artifact step reports no files for `.tmp/windows-launcher-*/`; the run artifact listing confirms no Windows archive in the #419 and #435 evidence. Current #435 native alias records are preserved in structured job stdout, which was independently inspected; its acceptance does not rely on a nonexistent archive. Default hidden-directory exclusion is a plausible cause, not yet verified. The new alias sandbox is under OS TEMP and also needs an explicit evidence-only retention policy.

Acceptance:
- Establish why the actual uploader finds no files on a disposable hosted Windows run.
- Publish bounded useful native evidence with an explicit safe path, excluding gateway keys, credentials, live stores and directory links to the checkout.
- Verify the uploaded archive by downloading it, checking its contents and linking it to the exact tested head/run/job.
- Preserve stdout diagnostics and declared handling when a failed test leaves a process or link requiring later investigation.

Deferred as a pre-existing CI evidence-retention issue; #488 concerns a Gates deadline and is a different root cause. Review observation O2.
